statement: In Gemma 4 E2B (google/gemma-4-E2B-it rev 3e22461, transformers 5.20.2), large sampled perturbations (Gaussian, sd 50) of the residual stream at all non-final positions entering layers 15, 16, 25 or 34 left final-position logits exactly unchanged, while the same perturbations entering layers 5, 13 or 14 changed them (max |Δlogit| 17.7-36.4). Together with the implementation (layers >= 15 read only K/V stored by layers 13/14), this indicates non-final positions after layer 14 are causally inert for final-position outputs.
scope: Gemma 4 E2B text decoder, inputs shorter than the 512-token sliding window, no KV cache, fp32 compute; implementation in transformers 5.20.2

supporting_evidence.summary: Gaussian noise (sd 50) on all non-final positions: max|Δlogit| = 0.0 at layers 15/16/25/34 vs 17.7-36.4 at layers 5/13/14; 2 prompts; identical in two separate runs
code: layers >= num_layers - num_kv_shared_layers (=15) take K/V from shared_kv_states stored by the last non-shared layer of the same type (13 sliding, 14 full)

conditions: 2 prompts (10 and 15 tokens); noise sd 50 per coordinate; Runner hooks at resid_pre
verification_method: Deterministic perturbation test + source-code reading; preregistered as P-ARCH-1 in experiments/E001_arch/PREREG.md
uncertainty: Behaviour with KV cache / generation and inputs longer than the sliding window not tested; a different implementation (e.g. official JAX) could differ only if it diverges from the HF reference.

history.change: wording narrowed per AUDIT-001 (sampled perturbations; tested layers listed)

statement: Running Gemma 4 E2B layers 15-34 on the final position only reproduces full-sequence final-position logits (observed max |Δ| = 3.62e-5 in fp32 on 2 single-sequence prompts; batched equivalence not separately tested) and cut a batched forward from 64.3 s to 29.8 s on the lab host.
scope: Final-position metrics only; inputs ≤ 512 tokens; fp32 compute; 2-vCPU host

supporting_evidence.summary: lastonly_vs_full_maxabs 3.6e-5 and 3.1e-5; speed full 64.32 s vs 29.8 s (8x40 batch)

verification_method: Direct comparison with full run and with HF model() (runner vs HF max|Δ| 1.3e-5-3.9e-5)
uncertainty: Speed-up measured on a shared CPU (subagents active); exact factor is host-dependent.

statement: The google/gemma-4-E2B-it tokenizer does not prepend <bos> by default; without BOS, prompt perplexity and next-token predictions degrade severely (e.g. 'The capital of France is': prompt perplexity 2.3e7 and next-token top-1 ' France' without BOS vs 257 and ' Paris' with BOS).
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it tokenizer.json/tokenizer_config.json at rev 3e22461; transformers 5.20.2 AutoTokenizer

supporting_evidence.summary: default_adds_bos=false; 4 prompts, all with large ppl drop when BOS added

uncertainty: Only 4 prompts; chat template path adds BOS itself (generation was coherent).

statement: On a CPU without AVX512_BF16, bf16 storage with fp32 matmuls changed Gemma 4 E2B final-position logits relative to native bf16 compute by 0.42-0.65 (max abs) on 4 BOS-prefixed prompts and by 0.26-2.32 on the same prompts without BOS, without changing the top-1 token in 8/8 cases; all causal experiments in this lab use fp32 compute.
scope: 8 prompt variants, IT checkpoint, lab host
uncertainty: Small prompt set; effect on patching metrics not quantified.

statement: Under the logit lens (final RMSNorm → tied unembedding → softcap 30) applied to the final-position residual stream of Gemma 4 E2B-IT, the correct single-token answer to 60 correctly answered factual prompts first becomes top-1 at residual index 26-34 (median 28, bootstrap 95% CI [28, 29]); it stays top-1 at all subsequent layers (median fraction 1.0), and its median rank at indices 0-5 is ~1.1e5 of 262 144.
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it; 62 English factual prompts (32 landmark→city, 30 country→capital; 60 answered correctly); residual index k = input to layer k (35 = final residual); logit lens only (no tuned lens)

supporting_evidence.summary: P1-P3 of the preregistration passed; by kind: landmark median 28, capital 29

conditions: fp32 compute; BOS prepended; layers >= 15 computed on the final position only (exact for this metric, K-0002)
verification_method: Preregistered (E002 PREREG.md) logit-lens analysis; independent recomputation by AUDIT-001
uncertainty: Logit lens is known to be biased for early layers (tuned lens not trained), so 'not top-1 before layer 26' does not imply the answer is not linearly decodable earlier. Single prompt template per kind; IT checkpoint only (base run pending).

statement: In Gemma 4 E2B-IT factual recall on short prompts, the subject information that determines the answer reaches the final position through the K/V stored by layer 13 (read by KV-shared layers 15-34), not through the K/V stored by layer 14: replacing the corrupt run's layer-13 stored K/V by the clean one recovers a median 0.986 of the logit difference (subject-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [0.947, 0.995]) vs 0.017 [0.011, 0.025] for layer 14 (28 held-out pairs); the effect is carried by the subject-span positions (0.980) and not by template positions (0.006).
scope: google/gemma-4-E2B-it; two relations (landmark->city 12 pairs, country->capital 16 pairs) with single-token answers; prompts 7-14 tokens (far below the 512-token sliding window, so this distinguishes the two stored K/V tensors, not sliding vs full attention); counterfactual patching with logit-difference recovery

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P1-P3 pass on held-out pairs; NULL control max|r| 1.1e-6; R2-only (never used before) KV13_all 0.982 vs KV14_all 0.017
consistent precursor: last-subject resid patch recovery 0.595 at layer 13 vs 0.010 at layer 14
two non-Anthropic auditors: no implementation bug; conclusions bounded as here

conditions: fp32 compute, BOS, Runner(last_only_from=15) with kv_store hook replacing (key, value) tensors stored after layer 13/14 for all/selected positions; corrupt prompt = same template, different subject, equal length
verification_method: Preregistered held-out test (E006 PREREG.md) + subject-clustered bootstrap + independent dual-model audit
uncertainty: Two templates/relations only; short prompts; IT checkpoint only; R1 held-out pairs share subjects with in-sample pairs. Layer-14 K/V may matter for other tasks or beyond the sliding window (H-011).

history.change: created from E006 after AUDIT-002 (from H-008)

statement: Among the 20 KV-shared layers of Gemma 4 E2B-IT, block-25 attention at the final position is the site where subject information enters the answer position in the tested factual-recall prompts, mainly via head 0: (i) sufficiency - patching only block 25's clean attention contribution into the corrupt run recovers a median 0.757 (subject-cluster CI [0.654, 0.826]) and is the largest of 20 single-layer attention patches in 28/28 held-out pairs; (ii) specificity - substituting the corrupt run's attention contribution leaves 0.227 of the logit difference at block 25 but >= 0.929 at every other KV-shared layer; (iii) head 0 of block 25 puts a median 0.88 of its final-query attention on the subject span (uniform baseline 0.17) and is the only head whose corruption matters (retained 0.37; other heads >= 0.98). It is NOT necessary in the ablation sense: replacing block 25's contribution by its mean over prompts retains 0.84 [0.815, 0.896], so the noising effect reflects conflicting (wrong-subject) content and a substantial backup route exists.
scope: as K-0006 (two relations, short prompts, IT checkpoint); head-level results from E006b (preregistered Q1, Q4 exploratory)

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P4 (sufficiency, argmax 28/28) and P5 (noising retains <= 0.5) pass
final-position residual recovery 0.056 entering block 25 vs 0.846 entering block 26
logit-lens answer emergence median residual index 28 (after block 25), consistent
preregistered Q1 (head-0 subject attention), Q2 (layer specificity) pass; Q3 (mean ablation <= 0.6) FAILS -> necessity claim withdrawn

contradicting_evidence.summary: MEAN_ATTN25 retained 0.84: block-25 subject-specific content is not necessary for recall

conditions: as K-0006; attention contribution = output of post_attention_layernorm at the final position
verification_method: Preregistered held-out tests E006 + E006b (specificity controls requested by AUDIT-002); independent dual-model audit of E006
uncertainty: Backup route under mean ablation unidentified (H-015). Single-head patching is non-additive through post-attention RMSNorm. Analogous to the attribute-extraction stage of Geva et al. 2023 (LIT02-065) but concentrated in one layer/head here; novelty vs prior Gemma 3n/4 analyses not established (LIT-06 abstract screening found no mechanistic study of shared-KV routing). E006b not yet externally audited.

E006b: added head-level + specificity evidence; withdrew 'necessary' reading of noising after mean-ablation control failed (Q3)

statement: In the HF transformers 5.20.2 implementation (which runs all 35 decoder layers at every prompt position), computing Gemma 4 E2B-IT layers 15-34 only at the final position during a single-sequence prefill leaves the final-position logits unchanged within 3.1e-5 (identical top-1 and top-10) for T = 64-1024 tokens, including T = 1024 beyond the 512-token sliding window, and reduces wall time by 1.8x (T=64), 2.4x (256), 2.7x (512) and 2.6-3.3x (1024; depending on summary statistic) on a 2-vCPU CPU with fp32 compute. At T = 2048 the full computation exceeded a 6.8 GB process RSS guard while the reduced one completed (58 s, sampled peak RSS 6.34 GB).
scope: single sequence, batch 1, CPU (AVX-512F, no bf16 GEMM), fp32 compute with bf16 weights, final-position output only (first generated token); decode with KV cache, batching and GPU not measured; energy not measurable in this sandbox

supporting_evidence.summary: preregistered P1 exactness, P2 >=2x for T>=256, P4 trend pass; T=2048 FULL missing (RSS guard)
exploratory: SKIP at T=2048 completes; FULL vs SKIP peak RSS growth at T=1024 0.35 vs 0.12 GB (allocator-order confounded)
K-0001/K-0002: non-final positions inert after layer 14

conditions: Runner.forward(logits='last') vs Runner.forward(last_only_from=15, allow_long=True); 1 warm-up + 3 interleaved repeats; shared host (timing noise: FULL T=1024 runs 61-85 s)
verification_method: Preregistered E007 (PREREG.md); transformers source inspected (Gemma4TextModel loops all layers; logits_to_keep only slices lm_head)
uncertainty: Preregistered cost model was wrong in one respect (it ignored that SKIP also drops the TxT attention of layers 15-34), so the 3.30x 'bound' (P3) is not a valid test; timing variance is large on the shared host; the saving is an implementation property already exploited by Google's on-device runtimes per Gemma 3n materials (not verified against a primary source).
